bullets.title: AI infrastructure selloff: semis crater on Anthropic slowdown call; NVDA -3.4%, AMD -6.3%, MRVL -9%
bullets.body: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei urged a slowdown in frontier AI development citing recursive self-improvement and rogue agent risks, triggering a broad AI infrastructure selloff. NVDA -3.4% (also in talks to invest up to $10B in Anthropic IPO), AMD -6.3%, MRVL -9.0%, AVGO -4.1%, ORCL -5.6%. Analysts broadly view voluntary pacing as unlikely without global coordination given US-China competitive pressure; Wells Fargo notes physical permitting/power constraints are the more likely capex cycle extender.

bullets.title: PLTR: UBS raises PT to $250 from $220, calls it best-positioned AI enabler at 51x '27 FCF
bullets.body: UBS raised its Palantir PT to $250 from $220 (based on 53x 2028 FCF) after AIPcon feedback reinforced the demand-outstrips-supply thesis. IT executives consistently expressed desire to control their AI stack (sovereign AI), customers deploying across multiple verticals, and no competitive pushback heard from models or data software peers. 2027 FCF multiple of 51x sits well below Snowflake and CrowdStrike despite a 63% 3-year revenue CAGR.

bullets.title: EBAY: Morgan Stanley reiterates Overweight, raises conviction on Depop; PT $127
bullets.body: Since the Depop acquisition closed July 30, Depop added 54% more WAUs than rival Vinted despite 46% fewer downloads, with a 48% download-to-WAU conversion vs Vinted's 17%. MS now sees 'relative peace' (50% odds) rather than a marketing arms race as the most likely FY27 outcome, reducing risk that FY27 EBIT guidance comes in at low-single-digits; mid-single-digit growth now seen as more likely. Reiterated as favorite SMID eCommerce name with PT $127.

bullets.title: HPE: Evercore ISI downgrades to In Line after 160% YTD gain; stock -10.8%
bullets.body: Evercore ISI downgraded HPE from Outperform to In Line citing share price appreciation and a mixed outlook; the stock fell 10.8% on the session after being up ~160% YTD. Wolfe Research also resumed coverage with a more cautious tone.

bullets.title: AFRM: Wolfe Research upgrades to Outperform from Peer Perform on strong FQ4 setup
bullets.body: Wolfe Research upgraded Affirm to Outperform from Peer Perform, citing a favorable setup following strong FQ4 results. No specific price target disclosed in the summary.

bullets.title: RBLX: +12.7% on new game formats and standalone app announcements
bullets.body: Roblox surged 12.7% after announcing new game formats and standalone app options across mobile, PC, and consoles, driving RBLX to be one of the main contributors to the S&P 1500 Communications Services Index's +2.8% gain on the day.

bullets.title: FOXA: Citizens initiates at Outperform, TP $95; Roku acquisition adds digital distribution
bullets.body: Citizens Financial initiated Fox Corp at Outperform with a $95 price target, citing the Roku acquisition as adding strong digital distribution. FOXA gained +3.9% on the session. Broadcasting segment was up 3.4% on the day largely on FOXA strength.

bullets.title: CHTR: Wolfe downgrades to Underperform; Morgan Stanley resumes Equal-Weight at $150 PT
bullets.body: Charter Communications was double-downgraded in a single session: Wolfe Research cut to Underperform and Morgan Stanley resumed coverage at Equal-Weight with a $150 price target.

bullets.title: DT (Dynatrace): UBS Buy $65 PT and Wolfe Outperform $65 PT; AI monetization still nascent in FY27 guide
bullets.body: Both UBS and Wolfe Research maintain positive views on DT at a $65 PT. Management flagged three AI monetization levers (incremental telemetry, observability for AI workloads, agentic workflows) but described AI contribution to FY27 ARR guidance as 'very little.' Core growth is driven by DPS renewals (~70% in 2H) and Logs consumption at $200M annualized; NRR expected to uptick in 2H but not step-function higher.

bullets.title: CLS: -8.8% on CFO transition; new CFO effective Oct 1
bullets.body: Celestica fell 8.8% (7.1% in Canadian trading) after the company announced its CFO has been appointed Group President and a new CFO will take over effective October 1. No earnings or guidance revision accompanied the announcement.

bullets.title: ORCL: Larry Ellison cancels $7.5B 10b5-1 stock sale plan; stock -3.7% on AI selloff
bullets.body: Larry Ellison canceled his plan to sell up to $7.5B of Oracle stock via a 10b5-1 plan; Oracle still declined 3.7% in sympathy with the broader AI infrastructure selloff.

bullets.title: EQIX/DLR/HUT: Data center REITs and HPC names hit hard on AI slowdown; EQIX -3.8%, DLR ~-5%, HUT -7.6%
bullets.body: Frontier LLM CEO calls for slower AI development triggered a data center REIT selloff: DLR fell ~5%, EQIX -3.8%, and HPC names HUT and WULF declined sharply. Analysts broadly view the weakness as overdone with Sunbelt fundamentals described as steady; IREN was upgraded to Overweight at JPMorgan with a $65 target despite being -1.5% on the day.

bullets.title: ADSK: Cantor Fitzgerald initiates at Neutral, $215 PT — implying 6% downside vs $229
bullets.body: Cantor Fitzgerald initiated Autodesk at Neutral with a $215 price target, implying ~6% downside from the $228.93 price at initiation. This is well below the FactSet consensus PT of $315.42 (range $265-$375).

bullets.title: DKNG: Iowa August sports betting GGR -11% Y/Y; hold rate compression across operators
bullets.body: Iowa August sports betting GGR fell 22% Y/Y statewide with the hold rate at 9.2% (-290bps Y/Y). DraftKings specifically saw GGR -11% Y/Y on +4% handle, with a hold rate of 10.3% (-180bps Y/Y). FanDuel GGR -33% Y/Y; BetMGM GGR -57% Y/Y. Casino GGR tracked -9.7% Y/Y for 3QTD. Fanatics was the only share gainer with GGR +27% Y/Y on +89% handle.

bullets.title: GOOGL/NOW: Bought on AI dislocation by Daniel & Collins; bullish on long-term AI optionality
bullets.body: Vincent Daniel and Porter Collins (of 'The Big Short' fame) disclosed they purchased GOOGL and NOW during AI-related weakness and remain long-term holds. They are cautious on AI capex ROI broadly but see GOOGL and NOW as best-positioned beneficiaries of the AI infrastructure buildout at dislocation prices.

bullets.title: SMTC: 1.6T ramp driving GM to 64%+ with 70% OPM target by Oct/Nov analyst day
bullets.body: Semtech IR notes Q3 guidance at 63.9% GM mid-point, with 1.6T products carrying 2x ASP vs 800G and highest GMs at ~70%. Company targeting 50% share in the 1.6T TIA/driver market; already above 50% at 800G. Content ASP ~$20 at 1.6T vs high-single-digits at 800G. 70% GM target seen achievable by the October/November analyst meeting.

bullets.title: NVDA: In talks to invest ~$10B in Anthropic IPO; Anthropic faces model restrictions at NVDA/PLTR
bullets.body: NVDA is reportedly in discussions to invest up to $10B as an anchor investor in Anthropic's upcoming IPO. Separately, Anthropic faces model-use restrictions at NVDA, PLTR, and Booz Allen Hamilton over data security concerns. Anthropic disclosed it will be profitable for a second consecutive quarter with gross margins >80%.

bullets.title: CRWV/NBIS: Roth survey on GPU-cloud demand durability vs hyperscalers — proprietary study available
bullets.body: Roth is fielding a 100-150 engineer survey targeting CoreWeave and competitor customers to assess GPU-cloud market share, speed/performance differentiation, and over/undercapacity risk. Results will be referenced in Roth Internet analyst Rohit Kulkarni's upcoming research on CRWV, NBIS, ORCL, AMZN, and NVDA.

bullets.title: ALAB/CRDO: Jefferies hosting OCP 2026 booth meetings Oct 13 with C-suite of both companies
bullets.body: Jefferies is hosting managed investor meetings at OCP 2026 Global Summit (Oct 13, San Jose) with Astera Labs CFO Des Lynch and Credo Semiconductor CEO Bill Brennan. Astera focuses on smart retimers and GPU booster cards; Credo on high-speed copper/optical interconnects for AI data infrastructure. Both are high-conviction AI infrastructure connectivity names.

bullets.title: MU/AAPL: Memory prices surging — DRAM +18.8% m/m, NAND +55-60%; Apple A20 Pro launch in tight supply
bullets.body: DDR5 RDIMM 32GB module pricing surged +18.8% m/m to $1,900. Apple's A20 Pro 2nm chip launch coincides with 58-63% DRAM contract price increases and 55-60% NAND price rises. OpenAI signed LOIs with Samsung and SK Hynix for next-gen memory for Stargate; Samsung's Taylor Texas fab hit 50K wafer/month capacity ahead of its 2027 ramp.
